## HealthCheck A simple health check endpoint to confirm whether the RESTful Booker API is up and running. Use this endpoint to verify service availability before executing other requests. --- ## Endpoint | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `GET` | | **URL** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/ping` | | **Authentication** | None | --- ## Request Details ### Headers No custom headers required. ### Query Parameters None. ### Request Body None. --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `1000` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds (used in tests) | --- ## Response ### Success — `201 Created` Returned when the API is healthy and running. | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Status Code** | `201 Created` | | **Content-Type** | `text/plain` | | **Body** | `Created` | **Example response body:** ``` Created ``` > ⚠️ Note: The API returns `201 Created` (not `200 OK`) for a successful health check. This is the expected behavior of the RESTful Booker API. --- ## Automated Tests This request includes the following post-response test scripts: | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts the response status code is `201 Created` | | **Test_2** | Asserts the response body exactly equals `"Created"` | | **Test_3** | Asserts the response time is below the `1000` environment variable value | --- ## Usage Run this request at the start of a collection run or before any booking operations to confirm the API is reachable. If this request fails, subsequent requests in the collection are likely to fail as well.

Iteration: 1 - create_token_valid_user_and_password
Request Description
# Auth - CreateToken This request authenticates a user against the RESTful Booker API and retrieves a session token. The token is required to perform protected operations — specifically the **PUT** and **PATCH** (update booking), **DELETE** (delete booking) endpoints under `/booking`. --- ## Endpoint ``` POST https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/auth ``` --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. It is the entry point for obtaining a token that will be used to authenticate subsequent requests. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | --- ## Request Body The request body must be a JSON object containing valid credentials. ``` json { "username": "admin", "password": "password123" } ``` | Field | Type | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `username` | string | `admin` | The username of the account to authenticate with | | `password` | string | `password123` | The password of the account to authenticate with | --- ## Response ### 200 OK A successful response returns a JSON object containing a single `token` property — an alphanumeric string used to authorize PUT and DELETE requests. ``` json { "token": "abc123def456" } ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `token` | string | Token for use in protected booking endpoints | --- ## Variables Upon a successful `200` response, the `token` value is **automatically extracted and saved** to the `token` collection variable. This makes it immediately available for use in subsequent requests such as: - `PUT /booking/:id` and `PATCH /booking/:id`— Update an existing booking - `DELETE /booking/:id` — Delete an existing booking The token is stored via the post-response script: ``` javascript pm.collectionVariables.set("token", resBody.token); ``` --- ## Notes - **Response time validation**: The response time is automatically validated against the `max_response_time` collection variable. - The token format is validated to be a non-empty alphanumeric string matching `/^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/`. - The response body is validated to be a JSON object containing exactly one key: `token`. --- ## Automated Tests This request includes the following post-response test scripts: | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts the response status code is `200 OK` | | **Test_2** | Asserts the response time is below the `1000` collection variable value | | **Test_3** | Asserts the response body is a JSON object with exactly one key: `token` | | **Test_4** | Asserts the `token` property is a non-empty alphanumeric string, and saves it to the `token` collection variable |

Iteration: 1 - create_token_invalid_user_and_password
Request Description
# Auth - CreateToken (Invalid Credentials) This request attempts to authenticate with invalid credentials against the RESTful Booker API. The API returns a `200 OK` status even for invalid credentials, but instead of a token, the response contains a `reason` field with the value `"Bad credentials"`. The `token` collection variable is cleared (set to empty string) to prevent stale tokens from being used in subsequent requests. --- ## Endpoint ``` POST https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/auth ``` --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | --- ## Request Body JSON object with invalid credentials: ``` json { "username": "{{invalid_username}}", "password": "{{invalid_password}}" } ``` | Field | Type | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `username` | string | `{{invalid_username}}` | An invalid username that does not match any account | | `password` | string | `{{invalid_password}}` | An invalid password that does not match any account | --- ## Response ### 200 OK Despite invalid credentials, the API returns `200 OK`. The response body contains a single `reason` field instead of a token. ``` json { "reason": "Bad credentials" } ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `reason` | string | Explains why authentication failed. Value is always `"Bad credentials"` for invalid credentials | --- ## Variables Upon receiving the response, the `token` collection variable is **cleared** (set to an empty string) to ensure no stale token from a previous successful authentication is accidentally used in subsequent requests. --- ## Notes - The API does **not** return a `4xx` error for invalid credentials — it always returns `200 OK`. - Response time is validated against the `max_response_time` collection variable. - The response body is validated to be a JSON object with exactly one key: `reason`. --- ## Automated Tests | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts the response status code is `200 OK` (API returns 200 even for invalid credentials) | | **Test_2** | Asserts the response time is below the `1000` collection variable value | | **Test_3** | Asserts the response body is a JSON object with exactly one key: `reason` | | **Test_4** | Asserts the `reason` property is a string with value `"Bad credentials"` | | **Test_5** | Clears the `token` collection variable by setting it to an empty string, ensuring no stale token is used in subsequent requests |

The API returns `200 OK` even in this case, but instead of a token, the response contains a `reason` field with the value `"Bad credentials"`. The `token` collection variable is cleared (set to empty string) to prevent stale tokens from being used in subsequent requests. --- ## Endpoint ``` POST https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/auth ``` --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | --- ## Request Body The request body contains only the `username` field. The `password` field is **intentionally missing** to test the API's handling of incomplete credentials. ``` json { "username": "admin" } ``` | Field | Type | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `username` | string | `admin` | A valid username — but authentication still fails due to the missing password | | `password` | — | _(omitted)_ | Intentionally not included in the request body | --- ## Response ### 200 OK Despite the missing `password` field, the API returns `200 OK`. The response body contains a single `reason` field instead of a token. ``` json { "reason": "Bad credentials" } ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `reason` | string | Explains why authentication failed. Value is `"Bad credentials"` when the password is missing | --- ## Variables Upon receiving the response, the `token` collection variable is **cleared** (set to an empty string) to ensure no stale token from a previous successful authentication is accidentally used in subsequent requests. --- ## Notes - The API does **not** return a `4xx` error for a missing password — it always returns `200 OK`. - Even a valid `username` is not sufficient — both fields are required for successful authentication. - Response time is validated against the `max_response_time` collection variable. - The response body is validated to be a JSON object with exactly one key: `reason`. --- ## Automated Tests | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts the response status code is `200 OK` (API returns 200 even for missing password) | | **Test_2** | Asserts the response time is below the `1000` collection variable value | | **Test_3** | Asserts the response body is a JSON object with exactly one key: `reason` | | **Test_4** | Asserts the `reason` property is a string with value `"Bad credentials"` | | **Test_5** | Clears the `token` collection variable by setting it to an empty string, ensuring no stale token is used in subsequent requests |

Request Description
# GetBookingIds Retrieves a list of all booking IDs currently stored in the system. Optionally, results can be filtered by guest name or check-in/check-out dates using query parameters. This request is used in the **Workflow 1: Full CRUD Lifecycle** folder as a confirmation step — both after creating a new booking (to verify it appears in the list) and after deleting one (to verify it no longer appears). --- ## Request Details | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `GET` | | **Endpoint** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking` | | **Authentication** | None required | | **Content-Type** | Not applicable | --- ## Query Parameters All query parameters are **optional**. When omitted, all booking IDs are returned. | Parameter | Type | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | String | Filter by guest first name | `Benny` | | `lastname` | String | Filter by guest last name | `Leffler` | | `checkin` | Date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | Filter bookings with check-in on or after this date | `2026-02-12` | | `checkout` | Date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | Filter bookings with check-out on or before this date | `2026-02-15` | --- ## Example Response — 200 OK ``` json [ { "bookingid": 60 }, { "bookingid": 223 }, { "bookingid": 132 }, { "bookingid": 480 } ] ``` --- ## Expected Status Codes | Status Code | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `200 OK` | Request succeeded; returns an array of booking ID objects | --- ## Test Coverage | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Status code is `200` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` ms | | `Test_3` | Response body is a non-empty array where each element contains an integer `bookingid` property | --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL for the RESTful Booker API | | `1000` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | | `Benny` | Collection | Guest first name used as an optional filter (disabled by default) | | `Leffler` | Collection | Guest last name used as an optional filter (disabled by default) | ---

# GetBookingIds (Filter by Check-in Date) Retrieves a list of booking IDs filtered by a specific check-in date. This is a read-only request that queries the RESTful Booker API and returns all bookings whose check-in date matches the provided value. --- ## HTTP Method & Endpoint ``` GET https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking?checkin=2026-02-12 ``` --- ## Query Parameters | Parameter | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `checkin` | `2026-02-12` | Date the guest is checking in (format: `YYYY-MM-DD`) | --- ## Successful Response **Status:** `200 OK` **Body:** A JSON array of booking ID objects. Each element has the following shape: ``` json [ { "bookingid": 1 }, { "bookingid": 2 } ] ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `bookingid` | `number` (integer) | Unique identifier of the booking | --- ## Test Coverage | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Asserts the response status code is `200` | | `Test_2` | Asserts the response time is below the `max_response_time` collection variable (parsed as an integer) | | `Test_3` | Asserts the response body is an array | | `Test_4` | Asserts each item in the array has a `bookingid` property that is an integer — **skipped if the array is empty** | --- ## Edge Cases - **Empty array:** If no bookings match the given check-in date, the API returns an empty array `[]`. In this case, a warning is logged to the console (`console.warn`) and `Test_4` is skipped using `pm.test.skip` to avoid false failures. - The `checkin` value must be a valid date string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Invalid or missing values may return an empty array or unexpected results.

# GetBooking (Valid ID) Retrieves a single booking by its `bookingid` and verifies the returned data matches what was submitted. Its own pre-request script creates a fresh, disposable booking first via `pm.sendRequest` - not dependent on `create_booking_valid` having already run, and not dependent on the shared demo's own existing data. --- ## Request | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | Method | `GET` | | Endpoint | `/booking/119` | | Auth | None required | --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `119` | Collection | ID of the booking to retrieve, set by this request's own pre-request script | | `Ethyl`, `Hirthe`, `750` | Collection | Expected values set by this request's own pre-request script, used to confirm the fetched booking matches | --- ## Response ### Success - `200 OK` Returns the full booking object for the given ID. ``` json { "firstname": "John", "lastname": "Smith", "totalprice": 450, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | string | First name of the guest | | `lastname` | string | Last name of the guest | | `totalprice` | integer | Total price of the booking | | `depositpaid` | boolean | Whether the deposit has been paid | | `bookingdates.checkin` | string | Check-in date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | | `bookingdates.checkout` | string | Check-out date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | | `additionalneeds` | string | Additional requirements | --- ## Test Coverage | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Status code is `200` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` ms | | `Test_3` | Response body is a JSON object with exactly 6 keys: `firstname`, `lastname`, `totalprice`, `depositpaid`, `bookingdates`, `additionalneeds` | | `Test_4` | `firstname` is a string matching the `Ethyl` collection variable | | `Test_5` | `lastname` is a string matching the `Hirthe` collection variable | | `Test_6` | `totalprice` is an integer matching the `750` collection variable | | `Test_7` | `depositpaid` is a boolean equal to `false` | | `Test_8` | `bookingdates` is an object with exactly 2 keys: `checkin` and `checkout` | | `Test_9` | `bookingdates.checkin` is a non-empty string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_10` | `bookingdates.checkout` is a non-empty string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_11` | `checkout` date is strictly later than `checkin` date | | `Test_12` | `additionalneeds` equals `"Breakfast"` | --- ## Notes - This request is self-sufficient: its own pre-request script creates the booking it then reads, rather than depending on `create_booking_valid` having already run first or on any specific data already existing on the shared demo instance.

## Get Booking by Invalid ID This request attempts to retrieve a booking using a **invalid booking ID**. It is used to verify that the API correctly handles non-existent booking IDs by returning a `404 Not Found` response. --- ### Endpoint ``` GET https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/invalid_booking_id ``` --- ### Variables | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `invalid_booking_id` | The booking ID used in the request — expected to be non-existent | --- ### Expected Behavior When an invalid `bookingid` is provided, the API should respond with: - **Status:** `404 Not Found` - **Content-Type:** `text/plain` - **Body:** Contains the text `"Not Found"` --- ### Tests 1. **Test_1 — Response status is 404 (Not Found)** Verifies that the HTTP response status code is `404`. 2. **Test_2 — Response time is below** **`max_response_time`** Verifies that the response time is below the threshold defined in the `max_response_time` collection variable. 3. **Test_3 — Response body is not empty and contains "Not Found"** Verifies that: - The `Content-Type` header includes `text/plain` - The response body is not empty - The response body includes the text `"Not Found"`

Request Description
# Booking - CreateBooking (Valid) This request creates a new booking in the RESTful Booker API using a valid, fully-populated request body. The `firstname`, `lastname`, and `totalprice` fields are randomly generated on each run using Postman dynamic variables. The remaining fields (`depositpaid`, `checkin`, `checkout`, `additionalneeds`) are hardcoded. On success, the API returns a `200 OK` with the new `bookingid` and the full `booking` object. The `bookingid` is automatically saved to the `bookingid` collection variable for use in subsequent requests. --- ## Endpoint ``` POST https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking ``` --- ## Authentication No authentication is required to create a booking. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | --- ## Pre-Request Script Before the request is sent, the pre-request script: - Generates a random `firstname` using `Lois` - Generates a random `lastname` using `Mante` - Generates a random integer `totalprice` (0–1000) using `850` - Uses hardcoded values for `depositpaid`, `checkin`, `checkout`, and `additionalneeds` - Dynamically builds and sets the request body - Saves all values to collection variables for use in post-response test validation --- ## Request Body ``` json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Ebert", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` | Field | Type | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | string | `Julien` | Randomly generated first name | | `lastname` | string | `Schuster` | Randomly generated last name | | `totalprice` | integer | `567` | Randomly generated price (0–1000) | | `depositpaid` | boolean | Hardcoded: `false` | Whether the deposit has been paid | | `bookingdates.checkin` | string | Hardcoded: `"2026-02-12"` | Check-in date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `bookingdates.checkout` | string | Hardcoded: `"2026-02-15"` | Check-out date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `additionalneeds` | string | Hardcoded: `"Breakfast"` | Any additional requirements | --- ## Response ### 200 OK A successful response returns a JSON object with two properties: `bookingid` and `booking`. ``` json { "bookingid": 1234, "booking": { "firstname": "John", "lastname": "Smith", "totalprice": 450, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } } ``` | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `bookingid` | integer | Unique ID of the newly created booking | | `booking` | object | Full booking object echoing back the submitted data | | `booking.firstname` | string | First name of the guest | | `booking.lastname` | string | Last name of the guest | | `booking.totalprice` | integer | Total price of the booking | | `booking.depositpaid` | boolean | Whether the deposit has been paid | | `booking.bookingdates.checkin` | string | Check-in date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | | `booking.bookingdates.checkout` | string | Check-out date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | | `booking.additionalneeds` | string | Additional requirements | --- ## Variables | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | Collection | Randomly generated — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `lastname` | Collection | Randomly generated — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `totalprice` | Collection | Randomly generated — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `depositpaid` | Collection | Hardcoded `false` — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `checkin` | Collection | Hardcoded `"2026-02-12"` — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `checkout` | Collection | Hardcoded `"2026-02-15"` — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `additionalneeds` | Collection | Hardcoded `"Breakfast"` — set by pre-request script, validated in tests | | `bookingid` | Environment | Saved from the response — used in subsequent GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE requests | --- ## Notes - Response time is validated against the `max_response_time` collection variable. - The `bookingid` is saved to the collection variable `bookingid` for use in downstream requests. - Date fields are validated to match the `YYYY-MM-DD` format. - `checkout` is validated to be strictly later than `checkin`. --- ## Automated Tests | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts the response status code is `200 OK` | | **Test_2** | Asserts the response time is below the `1000` collection variable value | | **Test_3** | Asserts the response body is a JSON object with exactly two keys: `bookingid` and `booking` | | **Test_4** | Asserts `bookingid` is an integer and saves it to the `bookingid` collection variable | | **Test_5** | Asserts `booking` is an object with exactly 6 keys: `firstname`, `lastname`, `totalprice`, `depositpaid`, `bookingdates`, `additionalneeds` | | **Test_6** | Asserts `booking.firstname` is a string matching the generated `Graciela` collection variable | | **Test_7** | Asserts `booking.lastname` is a string matching the generated `Ebert` collection variable | | **Test_8** | Asserts `booking.totalprice` is an integer matching the generated `745` collection variable | | **Test_9** | Asserts `booking.depositpaid` is a boolean matching the hardcoded `false` collection variable (`false`) | | **Test_10** | Asserts `booking.bookingdates` is an object with exactly 2 keys: `checkin` and `checkout` | | **Test_11** | Asserts `bookingdates.checkin` is a non-empty string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format matching `2026-02-12` | | **Test_12** | Asserts `bookingdates.checkout` is a non-empty string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format matching `2026-02-15` | | **Test_13** | Asserts `checkout` date is strictly greater than `checkin` date | | **Test_14** | Asserts `booking.additionalneeds` is a non-empty string matching the hardcoded `Breakfast` collection variable |

# Booking - CreateBooking (Missing Firstname) This request attempts to create a new booking in the RESTful Booker API with the `firstname` field intentionally omitted from the request body. The API responds with a `500 Internal Server Error` and a plain text body `"Internal Server Error"` — indicating that `firstname` is a required field. The `bookingid` collection variable is cleared after the test to prevent stale IDs from being used in subsequent requests. --- ## Endpoint ``` POST https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking ``` --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | --- ## Pre-Request Script Before the request is sent, the pre-request script: - Generates a random `lastname` using `Bechtelar` - Generates a random integer `totalprice` (0–1000) using `50` - Generates a random boolean `depositpaid` using `true` - `firstname` is **intentionally not generated or included** in the request body --- ## Request Body The `firstname` field is intentionally omitted to test the API's handling of an incomplete booking payload. ``` json { "lastname": "Ebert", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` | Field | Type | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | — | _(omitted)_ | Intentionally missing — required field | | `lastname` | string | `Kertzmann` | Randomly generated last name | | `totalprice` | integer | `803` | Randomly generated price (0–1000) | | `depositpaid` | boolean | `true` | Randomly generated boolean | | `bookingdates.checkin` | string | Hardcoded: `"2026-02-12"` | Check-in date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `bookingdates.checkout` | string | Hardcoded: `"2026-02-15"` | Check-out date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `additionalneeds` | string | Hardcoded: `"Breakfast"` | Additional needs for the booking | --- ## Expected Response **Status Code:** `500 Internal Server Error` **Content-Type:** `text/plain` **Body:** ``` Internal Server Error ``` --- ## Tests | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Asserts the response status code is `500 Internal Server Error` | | `Test_2` | Asserts the response time is below `max_response_time` (collection variable) | | `Test_3` | Asserts the `Content-Type` is `text/plain`, the body is not empty, and equals `"Internal Server Error"` | After the tests run, the `bookingid` collection variable is reset to an empty string `""` to avoid stale data in subsequent requests.

Request Description
# Booking - CreateBooking (Invalid date format) This request tests the API's behavior when booking dates are provided in an **invalid format** (`DD-MM-YYYY` instead of the expected `YYYY-MM-DD`). The API is expected to reject such input and return an error response (`400` or `500`). > ⚠️ **Known Bug** The API does not validate date formats and incorrectly returns `200 OK` instead of `400` or `500`. This is a bug that must be reported and fixed. --- ## Endpoint | Method | URL | | --- | --- | | `POST` | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com /booking` | --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. --- ## Request Headers | Key | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Indicates the request body is JSON | --- ## Pre-Request Script The following script dynamically generates values for `firstname`, `lastname`, `totalprice`, and `depositpaid` using Postman dynamic variables before each request execution: ``` javascript const firstname = pm.variables.replaceIn('Cole') const lastname = pm.variables.replaceIn('Cummings') const totalprice = parseInt(pm.variables.replaceIn('6'), 10); ``` > These variables are then injected into the request body via `Graciela`, `Ebert` and `745.` --- ## Request Body ``` json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Ebert", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "12-02-2026", "checkout": "15-02-2026" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` | Field | Type | Value / Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | `string` | `Graciela` (dynamic) | Randomly generated first name | | `lastname` | `string` | `Ebert` (dynamic) | Randomly generated last name | | `totalprice` | `number` | `745` (dynamic) | Randomly generated integer price | | `depositpaid` | `boolean` | `false` (dynamic) | Randomly generated boolean | | `bookingdates.checkin` | `string` | `"12-02-2026"` | ❌ **Wrong format** — uses `DD-MM-YYYY` instead of `YYYY-MM-DD` | | `bookingdates.checkout` | `string` | `"15-02-2026"` | ❌ **Wrong format** — uses `DD-MM-YYYY` instead of `YYYY-MM-DD` | | `additionalneeds` | `string` | `"Breakfast"` | Static additional request | --- ## Expected Response The API does not validate date formats: it accepts `DD-MM-YYYY` and returns `200 OK` with a full booking object instead of rejecting it. This test asserts that documented, current behavior directly, rather than an ideal response the API never actually sends. --- ## Automated Tests | Test Name | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1. API does not validate date format** | Asserts the response status is `200` - the known, verified bug behavior, not the `400`/`500` a validating API would return | | **Test_2. Response time is below max_response_time** | Asserts that `responseTime` is below the value of the `max_response_time` collection variable (parsed as integer) | | **Restore bookingid** | Sets the `bookingid` collection variable to an empty string `""` and asserts it equals `""`, ensuring a clean state after the test |

# Booking - CreateBooking (Checkout date before checkin) This request tests the API's behavior when the **checkout date is earlier than the checkin date** — specifically, `checkout: 2026-02-12` before `checkin: 2026-02-15`. The API is expected to validate the date order and reject the request with a `400` or `500` error response. > ⚠️ Known Bug The API does not validate date order and incorrectly returns `200 OK` instead of `400` or `500`. --- ## Endpoint | Method | URL | | --- | --- | | `POST` | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking` | --- ## Authentication No authentication is required for this request. --- ## Request Headers | Key | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Sets the format of payload you are sending | --- ## Pre-Request Script ``` javascript const firstname = pm.variables.replaceIn('Jayme'); const lastname = pm.variables.replaceIn('Veum'); const totalprice = parseInt(pm.variables.replaceIn('593'), 10); ``` This script dynamically generates request data before each run using Postman dynamic variables: - **`firstname`** — a random first name generated via `Rosalia` - **`lastname`** — a random last name generated via `Langosh` - **`totalprice`** — a random integer generated via `362`, parsed to an integer Note that `depositpaid` is hardcoded to `false` directly in the request body. --- ## Request Body ``` json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Ebert", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-15", "checkout": "2026-02-12" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` | Field | Type | Value / Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `firstname` | String | `Graciela` (pre-request script) | Randomly generated first name | | `lastname` | String | `Ebert` (pre-request script) | Randomly generated last name | | `totalprice` | Integer | `745` (pre-request script) | Randomly generated total price | | `depositpaid` | Boolean | `false` (hardcoded) | Whether a deposit has been paid | | `bookingdates.checkin` | String | `"2026-02-15"` (hardcoded) | Check-in date | | `bookingdates.checkout` | String | `"2026-02-12"` ⚠️ (hardcoded) | **Checkout is before checkin** — this is the invalid scenario being tested | | `additionalneeds` | String | `"Breakfast"` (hardcoded) | Any additional requirements for the booking | --- ## Expected Response The API does not validate date order: it accepts a checkout date before the checkin date and returns `200 OK` with a full booking object instead of rejecting it. This test asserts that documented, current behavior directly, rather than an ideal response the API never actually sends. --- ## Automated Tests | Test Name | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1. # UpdateBooking Performs a **full replacement** of an existing booking record using the `PUT /booking/:id` endpoint of the RESTful Booker API. All booking fields are overwritten in a single request. This request is used in the **full CRUD lifecycle workflow** as **Step 5**, immediately after the booking has been created and verified. --- ## Authentication Authentication is provided via a **Cookie header**: ``` Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60 ``` The `fd8b30247a7fb60` value is generated by the `create_token_valid_user_and_password` request and stored as a collection variable. > **Alternative:** The `Authorization: Basic` header can also be used instead of the Cookie. See the commented-out code in the pre-request script (Step 3). --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `131` | Collection (set by `create_booking_valid`) | ID of the booking to update | | `fd8b30247a7fb60` | Collection (set by `create_token_valid_user_and_password`) | Auth token for protected endpoints | | `Graciela` | Collection | Guest first name (unchanged in this update) | | `Bernhard` | Collection (set in pre-request script) | Randomly generated new last name | | `745` | Collection | Total price of the booking (unchanged) | | `false` | Collection | Whether deposit was paid (unchanged) | | `2026-02-12` | Collection | Check-in date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format (unchanged) | | `2026-02-15` | Collection | Check-out date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format (unchanged) | | `Breakfast` | Collection | Additional needs string (unchanged) | --- ## Pre-request Script Behaviour 1. **Prerequisite check** — asserts that `131` and `fd8b30247a7fb60` are already set as collection variables (fails fast if a prior step was skipped). 2. **Random lastname generation** — generates a new random last name using `Armstrong` and saves it to `Bernhard` for use in the request body and post-response assertions. --- ## Request Body A full booking object is sent as JSON. Only `lastname` is intentionally changed; all other fields carry their original values: ``` json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Bernhard", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `200 OK` The response body mirrors the full updated booking object (6 fields): ``` json { "firstname": "string", "lastname": "string (updated)", "totalprice": number, "depositpaid": boolean, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "YYYY-MM-DD", "checkout": "YYYY-MM-DD" }, "additionalneeds": "string" } ``` --- ## Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Status code is `200` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` | | `Test_3` | Response body is a valid JSON object with exactly 6 keys | | `Test_4` | `firstname` is unchanged and matches the stored value | | `Test_5` | `lastname` is updated and matches `Bernhard` (differs from original `Ebert`) | | `Test_6` | `totalprice` is unchanged and is an integer | | `Test_7` | `depositpaid` is unchanged and is a boolean | | `Test_8` | `bookingdates` is an object with exactly 2 keys (`checkin`, `checkout`) | | `Test_9` | `checkin` is unchanged, non-empty, and matches `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_10` | `checkout` is unchanged, non-empty, and matches `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_11` | `additionalneeds` is unchanged and matches the stored value |

Request Description
# UpdateBooking — Cookie Header Disabled (Negative Test) Attempts a **full booking update** (`PUT /booking/:id`) with the `Cookie` authentication header **intentionally disabled**. This is a **negative test** that verifies the API correctly rejects unauthenticated requests with a `403 Forbidden` response. --- ## Purpose This request validates that the RESTful Booker API enforces authentication on the `PUT /booking/:id` endpoint. By disabling the `Cookie` header, the request is sent without any credentials, and the expected outcome is a `403 Forbidden` error. --- ## Authentication | Method | Header | Status | |--------|--------|--------| | Cookie token | `Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | ⛔ **Disabled** | > The `Cookie` header is present in the request but **disabled**. No `Authorization` header is set either. # UpdateBooking — Invalid Token Negative test case for the `PUT /booking/:id` endpoint. Sends a full booking update with a **deliberately invalid authentication token** in the `Cookie` header. The API is expected to reject the request with a `403 Forbidden` response, confirming that the endpoint enforces token validation before allowing any modifications. --- ## Request Details | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `PUT` | | **Endpoint** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | | **Auth** | None (no auth helper) | | **Content-Type** | `application/json` | ### Authentication Authentication is passed via the `Cookie` header with a hardcoded invalid value: ``` Cookie: token=invalid_random_string ``` This simulates a scenario where a client presents a token that does not match any valid session on the server. > **Note:** An alternative approach (commented out in the pre-request script) is to set the `Cookie` header programmatically via `pm.request.headers.add(...)`. --- ## Request Body A complete booking payload is sent despite the invalid token, to confirm the server rejects the request at the auth layer before processing the body: ``` json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Bernhard", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-02-12", "checkout": "2026-02-15" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ``` --- ## Variables | Variable | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to update (set by a prior create request) | | `firstname` | Collection | First name of the guest | | `updated_lastname` | Pre-request script | Randomly generated last name (via `Kutch`) | | `totalprice` | Collection | Total price of the booking | | `depositpaid` | Collection | Whether a deposit has been paid | | `checkin` | Collection | Check-in date | | `checkout` | Collection | Check-out date | | `additionalneeds` | Collection | Any additional needs for the booking | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | --- ## Pre-request Script 1. **Prerequisite check** — Asserts that `bookingid` is set as a collection variable before the request is sent. 2. **Generate updated lastname** — Generates a random last name using `Kuhn` and stores it in `updated_lastname`. 3. _(Commented out)_ Alternative method to inject the `Cookie` header programmatically instead of using the static header. --- ## Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Response status is `403 Forbidden` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `max_response_time` (collection variable) | | `Test_3` | Response `Content-Type` is `text/plain`; body is not empty and equals `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `403 Forbidden` **Body:** ``` Forbidden ``` --- ## Related Requests - `update_booking_valid` — Same endpoint with a valid token; expects `200 OK` - `update_booking_expired_token` — Same endpoint with an expired token; expects `403 Forbidden` - `update_booking_invalid_id` — Same endpoint with an invalid booking ID; expects `405 Method Not Allowed` ---

# UpdateBooking — Invalid Booking ID This is a **negative test** for the `PUT /booking/:id` endpoint. It verifies that the API returns `405 Method Not Allowed` when an invalid or non-existent booking ID (e.g. `999999`) is provided. The test confirms that the server correctly rejects the request and returns a plain-text error body. --- ## Request Details | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `PUT` | | **URL** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | | **Content-Type** | `application/json` | | **Cookie** | `token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | --- ## Pre-request Script Summary The pre-request script performs the following steps: 1. **Sets an invalid booking ID** — `bookingid` is set to `999999`, a non-existent ID, to intentionally trigger an error response from the API. 2. **Generates a random last name** — `updated_lastname` is assigned a random value using `Bartoletti` via `pm.variables.replaceIn`. 3. **Alternative Cookie header approach** — There is a commented-out block that demonstrates an alternative way to attach the auth token using `pm.request.headers.add` with a `Cookie: token=...` header, instead of relying on the static header defined in the request. --- ## Test Assertions | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Response status is `405` (Method Not Allowed) | | **Test_2** | Response time is below the `max_response_time` collection variable | | **Test_3** | Response body is not empty, `Content-Type` header includes `text/plain`, and body equals `"Method Not Allowed"` | --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Set to `999999` in the pre-request script (invalid/non-existent ID) | | `token` | Auth token used in the Cookie header | | `firstname` | Booking first name (part of request body) | | `updated_lastname` | Randomly generated last name for the update payload | | `totalprice` | Total price for the booking | | `depositpaid` | Boolean indicating whether deposit was paid | | `checkin` | Check-in date | | `checkout` | Check-out date | | `additionalneeds` | Any additional needs for the booking | --- ## Expected Response | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Status** | `405 Method Not Allowed` | | **Body** | `Method Not Allowed` (plain text) |

# PartialUpdateBooking Partially updates an existing booking by sending only the fields that need to change. Uses the HTTP `PATCH` method, which applies a partial modification — only the supplied fields are updated; all other fields retain their current values. This request updates **`firstname`** **only** and verifies that all other booking fields remain unchanged. --- ## Authentication Requires a valid session token passed via the `Cookie` header: ``` Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60 ``` The `fd8b30247a7fb60` variable is populated by the `create_token_valid_user_and_password` request earlier in the workflow. > **Alternative:** The token can also be passed as an `Authorization: Bearer fd8b30247a7fb60` header. See the commented-out code in the pre-request script (STEP 3). --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `131` | Collection | ID of the booking to partially update (set by `create_booking_valid`) | | `fd8b30247a7fb60` | Collection | Auth token (set by `create_token_valid_user_and_password`) | | `Kaelyn` | Collection | Randomly generated firstname set in the pre-request script | --- ## Request Body Only the field(s) to be updated are included in the body: ``` json { "firstname": "Kaelyn" } ``` --- ## Pre-request Script Summary 1. **Prerequisites check** — Asserts that `bookingid` and `token` collection variables are set before the request is sent. 2. **Generate random firstname** — Uses `Cecelia` to generate a new firstname and stores it in `partial_updated_firstname` for use in the request body and post-response assertions. --- ## Post-response Tests | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Status code is `200 OK` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` | | `Test_3` | Response body is valid JSON with exactly 6 expected keys | | `Test_4` | `firstname` equals the newly generated `partial_updated_firstname` value | | `Test_5` | `lastname` is **unchanged** from the original booking | | `Test_6` | `totalprice` is **unchanged** from the original booking | | `Test_7` | `depositpaid` is **unchanged** from the original booking | | `Test_8` | `bookingdates` object is present with `checkin` and `checkout` keys | | `Test_9` | `checkin` date is **unchanged** and matches `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_10` | `checkout` date is **unchanged** and matches `YYYY-MM-DD` format | | `Test_11` | `additionalneeds` is **unchanged** from the original booking | --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `200 OK` ``` json { "firstname": "<newly generated firstname>", "lastname": "<original lastname>", "totalprice": <original totalprice>, "depositpaid": <original depositpaid>, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "<original checkin>", "checkout": "<original checkout>" }, "additionalneeds": "<original additionalneeds>" } ``` --- ## Workflow Position This request is **Step 7** in _Workflow 1: Full CRUD Lifecycle_. It is followed by a `GET /booking/:id` request (Step 8) that re-fetches the booking to confirm the partial update was applied correctly.

# PartialUpdateBooking (Invalid date format) This is a **negative test** for the `PATCH /booking/:id` endpoint. It submits booking dates in an **invalid format** (`DD/MM/YYYY` instead of the required `YYYY-MM-DD`) and verifies how the API handles the malformed input. Despite the invalid date format, the RESTful Booker API currently returns **200 OK** — this request documents and validates that (potentially unexpected) behaviour. --- ## Endpoint `PATCH https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` --- ## Purpose - Verify API behaviour when `checkin` and `checkout` dates are submitted in an incorrect format (`DD/MM/YYYY`). - Confirm that only `firstname` is partially updated; all other fields remain unchanged. - Assert the exact, verified values the API actually returns for this malformed input, documenting its lack of input validation on date fields directly rather than leaving these two tests permanently red. --- ## Authentication Uses a session token passed via the `Cookie` header: ``` Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60 ``` The `fd8b30247a7fb60` variable must be set before this request runs (e.g. by executing `create_token_valid_user_and_password` first). --- ## Request Body ``` json { "bookingdates": { "checkin": "12/02/2026", "checkout": "15/02/2026" } } ``` > ⚠️ Dates are intentionally in `DD/MM/YYYY` format — this is the invalid input being tested. --- ## Required Variables | Variable | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to partially update | | `token` | Collection | Auth token from the `/auth` endpoint | | `partial_updated_firstname` | Collection | Expected `firstname` value after partial update | | `lastname` | Collection | Original `lastname` (should remain unchanged) | | `totalprice` | Collection | Original `totalprice` (should remain unchanged) | | `depositpaid` | Collection | Original `depositpaid` (should remain unchanged) | | `checkin` | Collection | Original `checkin` date (should remain unchanged) | | `checkout` | Collection | Original `checkout` date (should remain unchanged) | | `additionalneeds` | Collection | Original `additionalneeds` (should remain unchanged) | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in ms | --- ## Pre-request Script Validates that `bookingid` and `token` collection variables are set before the request is sent. --- ## Tests (Post-response) | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Status code is `200` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `max_response_time` | | `Test_3` | Response body is a valid JSON object with exactly 6 expected keys | | `Test_4` | `firstname` reflects the partially updated value (`partial_updated_firstname`) | | `Test_5` | `lastname` is unchanged | | `Test_6` | `totalprice` is unchanged | | `Test_7` | `depositpaid` is unchanged | | `Test_8` | `bookingdates` is an object with `checkin` and `checkout` keys | | `Test_9` | `checkin` equals `"2026-12-02"` - the API's actual, verified reinterpretation of `12/02/2026`, not the original date | | `Test_10` | `checkout` equals `"0NaN-aN-aN"` - the API's actual, verified (garbled) output for `15/02/2026`, not the original date | | `Test_11` | `additionalneeds` is unchanged | > ℹ️ **Tests 9 and 10 assert the API's real, verified output for this malformed input directly** rather than an ideal rejection it never sends - the same treatment already used elsewhere in this collection for the other documented date/price validation gaps (see `04_Booking - Create Operations`). --- ## Expected Response (200 OK) ``` json { "firstname": "Kaelyn", "lastname": "Bernhard", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-12-02", "checkout": "0NaN-aN-aN" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ```

# PartialUpdateBooking — Cookie Header Disabled (Negative Test) This is a **negative test** for the `PATCH /booking/:id` endpoint. It verifies that the API correctly rejects a partial update request when the `Cookie` authentication header is **disabled**, returning a `403 Forbidden` response. --- ## Endpoint | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Method | `PATCH` | | URL | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | | Auth | None (Cookie header intentionally disabled) | --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | Enabled | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | ✅ Yes | Required for JSON body | | `Cookie` | `token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | ❌ No | Auth header — **disabled** to trigger 403 | --- ## Request Body ``` json { "firstname": "Robin" } ``` Only the `firstname` field is sent. The value is randomly generated in the pre-request script and stored in `Robin`. --- ## Variables | Variable | Source | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Environment | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to partially update (set by a prior create request) | | `token` | Collection | Auth token (set by a prior auth request) | | `partial_updated_firstname` | Collection (set in pre-request) | Randomly generated first name used in the request body | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | --- ## Pre-Request Script Summary 1. **Validates prerequisites** — asserts that `bookingid` and `token` collection variables are set before the request runs. 2. **Generates a random** **`firstname`** — uses `Forest` to produce a new value and stores it in `partial_updated_firstname` for use in the body and post-response verification. --- ## Post-Response Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Response status is `403 Forbidden` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` ms | | `Test_3` | Response body is `text/plain`, non-empty, and equals `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `403 Forbidden` **Content-Type:** `text/plain` **Body:** ``` Forbidden ``` --- ## Purpose This request confirms that the RESTful Booker API enforces authentication on the `PATCH /booking/:id` endpoint. When the `Cookie: token=...` header is absent (disabled), the server must respond with `403 Forbidden` — not a `200 OK` or any other success code.

# PartialUpdateBooking — Expired Token (403 Forbidden) This is a **negative test** that verifies the API correctly rejects a `PATCH /booking/:id` request when an **expired or invalid authentication token** is supplied via the `Cookie` header. The expected outcome is a `403 Forbidden` response, confirming that the server enforces token validity on partial update operations. --- ## Endpoint ``` PATCH https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131 ``` --- ## Authentication | Method | Header | Value | | --- | --- | --- | | Cookie | `Cookie` | `token=` | > ⚠️ The token value `ccb59d3efd94c3a` used in this request is intentionally **expired/invalid** to trigger the `403 Forbidden` response. No `Authorization` header is used. Auth type is set to **No Auth**. --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Required for JSON body | | `Cookie` | `token=ccb59d3efd94c3a` | Expired/invalid token — triggers 403 | --- ## Request Body ``` json { "firstname": "Robin" } ``` Only `firstname` is sent in the body. The value is driven by the `Robin` collection variable. --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to partially update | | `partial_updated_firstname` | Collection | First name value to send in the PATCH body | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time (ms) for performance assertion | --- ## Pre-request Script Summary 1. **Prerequisite check** — Asserts that `bookingid` collection variable is defined before the request is sent. 2. **Random lastname generation** — Generates a random last name using `Rath` and stores it in `updated_lastname` (available for downstream use). 3. _(Commented out)_ An alternative approach to set the `Cookie` header programmatically via `pm.request.headers.add()` is included as a reference. --- ## Post-response Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Response status is `403 Forbidden` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `1000` ms | | `Test_3` | Response `Content-Type` is `text/plain`; body is not empty and equals `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `403 Forbidden` **Body:** ``` Forbidden ``` **Content-Type:** `text/plain` --- ## Notes - This request is part of the **Bookings - Update Operations** folder in the `RESTful_Booker` collection. - It is a companion to `partial_update_booking_valid`, which uses a valid token and expects a `200 OK`. - To obtain a valid token, run `create_token_valid_user_and_password` first (see **Workflow 1: Full CRUD Lifecycle**).

# PartialUpdateBooking — Invalid Token (Negative Test) ## Purpose This request verifies that the **PATCH /booking/:id** endpoint correctly **rejects** partial update attempts made with an **invalid (random string) authentication token**, returning `403 Forbidden`. --- ## Endpoint | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `PATCH` | | **URL** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | | **Auth** | None (auth is passed via `Cookie` header) | --- ## Request Headers | Header | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Indicates the request body is JSON | | `Cookie` | `token=invalid_random_string` | Intentionally invalid token — expected to be rejected by the server | --- ## Request Body Only the `firstname` field is sent in the partial update payload: ``` json { "firstname": "Robin" } ``` | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `Robin` | The new first name value to attempt to apply | --- ## Required Variables | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to attempt to update | | `partial_updated_firstname` | Collection | First name value used in the partial update body | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | --- ## Pre-request Script Summary 1. **Prerequisite check** — Asserts that `bookingid` collection variable is defined before the request is sent. 2. **Random lastname generation** — Generates a random last name using `Spencer` and stores it in `updated_lastname` (for potential reuse or verification). 3. _(Commented out)_ An alternative approach to set the `Cookie` header programmatically via `pm.request.headers.add()` is included as a reference. --- ## Test Script Summary | Test | Description | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Asserts response status is `403 Forbidden` | | **Test_2** | Asserts response time is below `max_response_time` (collection variable) | | **Test_3** | Asserts `Content-Type` is `text/plain`, body is not empty, and body equals `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Expected Response | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Status** | `403 Forbidden` | | **Content-Type** | `text/plain` | | **Body** | `Forbidden` | --- ## Notes - This is a **negative/security test** — the request is intentionally crafted to fail authentication. - The `Cookie` header uses a hardcoded `invalid_random_string` value to simulate a tampered or forged token. - Compare with `partial_update_booking_valid` (which uses a valid token) and `partial_update_booking_expired_token` (which uses an expired token) to understand the full auth validation coverage.

# UpdateBooking (Invalid date format) This is a **negative test** for the `PUT /booking/:id` endpoint - the PUT counterpart to `partial_update_booking_invalid_date_format`. It submits booking dates in an **invalid format** (`DD/MM/YYYY` instead of the required `YYYY-MM-DD`) and verifies how the API handles the malformed input. Despite the invalid date format, the RESTful Booker API currently returns **200 OK** - and (verified directly, 2026-08-14) mangles the dates identically to how the PATCH endpoint does: this request documents and validates that (potentially unexpected) behaviour for PUT specifically. Deliberately placed **last** in this folder, after every other request that depends on this booking's `bookingdates` still being pristine (e.g. `partial_update_booking_valid`'s own "unchanged" assertions) - this request permanently corrupts those dates on the shared record, same as `partial_update_booking_invalid_date_format` already does for PATCH. --- ## Endpoint `PUT https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` --- ## Purpose - Verify API behaviour when `checkin` and `checkout` dates are submitted in an incorrect format (`DD/MM/YYYY`) on a full update. - Confirm every other field is a plain echo of what was sent (a PUT resends the whole record, unlike PATCH). - Assert the exact, verified values the API actually returns for this malformed input, documenting its lack of input validation on date fields directly rather than leaving this test permanently red. --- ## Authentication Uses a session token passed via the `Cookie` header: ``` Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60 ``` The `fd8b30247a7fb60` variable must be set before this request runs (e.g. by executing `create_token_valid_user_and_password` first). --- ## Expected Response (200 OK) ```json { "firstname": "Graciela", "lastname": "Bernhard", "totalprice": 745, "depositpaid": false, "bookingdates": { "checkin": "2026-12-02", "checkout": "0NaN-aN-aN" }, "additionalneeds": "Breakfast" } ```

# DeleteBooking Deletes an existing booking by its ID. This is a **protected endpoint** — a valid session token must be provided via the `Cookie` header. Returns `201 Created` with a plain-text body of `Created` on success. --- ## Authentication Authentication is passed via the `Cookie` header: ``` Cookie: token=fd8b30247a7fb60 ``` The `fd8b30247a7fb60` collection variable must be populated before this request runs (e.g. by executing `create_token_valid_user_and_password` first). > **Alternative:** The commented-out code in the pre-request script shows how to set the `Cookie` header programmatically instead of using a static header. --- ## Path Variables | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `131` | The ID of the booking to delete. Set automatically by `create_booking_valid`. | --- ## Headers | Key | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Declares the request content type. | | `Cookie` | `token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | Passes the session token for authorisation. Can be set statically (as here) or programmatically via the pre-request script. | --- ## Pre-request Script Validates that the required collection variables are set before the request is sent: - `bookingid` — must not be `undefined` - `token` — must not be `undefined` If either variable is missing, the prerequisite test will fail and alert you before the request fires. --- ## Tests (Post-response) | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1. Status code is 201` | Response status must be `201 Created` | | `Test_2. Response time is below max_response_time` | Response time must be below the `1000` collection variable (ms) | | `Test_3. Response body is JSON` | `Content-Type` contains `text/plain`; body is non-empty and equals `"Created"` | --- ## Expected Response | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Status | `201 Created` | | Content-Type | `text/plain; charset=utf-8` | | Body | `Created` | --- ## Required Collection Variables | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | ID of the booking to delete | | `token` | Session token obtained from the `/auth` endpoint | | `max_response_time` | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | --- ## Usage in Workflow This request is **Step 9** of _Workflow 1: Full CRUD Lifecycle_. It deletes the booking created earlier in the workflow. After this request, `get_booking_by_invalid_id` (Step 10) confirms the booking no longer exists by asserting a `404 Not Found` response.

# DeleteBooking (Cookie Header Disabled) Attempts to delete an existing booking **without** a valid `Cookie` authentication header. The `Cookie` header is present in the request but **disabled**, so no token is sent. This is a **negative / security test** that verifies the API correctly rejects unauthenticated delete requests with a `403 Forbidden` response. --- ## Endpoint `DELETE https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` --- ## Purpose Validates that the RESTful Booker API enforces authentication on the `DELETE /booking/:id` endpoint. When the `Cookie: token=` header is omitted or disabled, the API must refuse the request and return `403 Forbidden`. --- ## Authentication | Header | Value | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | ✅ Enabled | | `Cookie` | `token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | ❌ Disabled | > **Note:** The `Cookie` header is intentionally disabled to simulate a request made without authentication. To send an authenticated delete request, enable the `Cookie` header or use the `Authorization` header alternative (see pre-request script comments). --- ## Required Variables | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `base_url` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `bookingid` | Collection | ID of the booking to delete | | `token` | Collection | Auth token obtained from `POST /auth` | | `max_response_time` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time (ms) | --- ## Pre-request Script Validates that `bookingid` and `token` collection variables are set before the request is sent. Also includes a commented-out alternative for programmatically adding the `Cookie` header via script. --- ## Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` | Response status is `403 Forbidden` | | `Test_2` | Response time is below `max_response_time` | | `Test_3` | Response body is `"Forbidden"` (plain text, non-empty) | --- ## Expected Response **Status:** `403 Forbidden` **Content-Type:** `text/plain` **Body:** ``` Forbidden ``` --- ## Contrast: Authenticated Delete For the successful (authenticated) delete flow, see `delete_booking_valid` in the same folder, which sends the `Cookie` header enabled and expects a `201 Created` response.

# DeleteBooking (Expired Token) This request is a **negative/security test** that verifies the API correctly rejects a delete operation when an **expired or invalid authentication token** is provided. The expected outcome is a `403 Forbidden` response, confirming that the server enforces token validity before allowing destructive operations. --- ## Method & Endpoint | Method | Endpoint | | --- | --- | | `DELETE` | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | --- ## Authentication Authentication is provided via a hardcoded **expired token** in the `Cookie` header: ``` Cookie: token=ccb59d3efd94c3a ``` This token is **intentionally expired/invalid** to trigger the `403 Forbidden` response. No valid token is used in this request by design. --- ## Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | | `Cookie` | `token=ccb59d3efd94c3a` | --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `131` | ID of the booking to be deleted (set by a prior create request) | --- ## Pre-request Script Summary Before the request is sent, the pre-request script performs a prerequisite check: - **Validates** that the `bookingid` collection variable is defined and not `undefined`. If this check fails, it signals that the test environment is not properly set up and the request should not proceed. --- ## Test Summary Three automated tests run after the response is received: | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | **Test_1** | Response status code is `403` (Forbidden) | | **Test_2** | Response time is below the `max_response_time` collection variable (in ms) | | **Test_3** | Response `Content-Type` is `text/plain`, body is not empty, and body text equals `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Expected Response | Property | Expected Value | | --- | --- | | **Status Code** | `403 Forbidden` | | **Body** | `Forbidden` | | **Content-Type** | `text/plain` | --- ## Notes - This is a **negative/security test** — it is expected to fail authentication by design. - It confirms that the API does **not** allow booking deletion with an expired or invalid token. - To test a successful deletion, use the `delete_booking_valid` request, which uses a valid token obtained from the authentication endpoint.

# DeleteBooking (Invalid Token) This is a **negative test** that sends a `DELETE` request to `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` using an **intentionally invalid token** in the `Cookie` header. The goal is to verify that the API correctly rejects unauthorised deletion attempts and returns a `403 Forbidden` response. --- ## Endpoint | Method | URL | | --- | --- | | `DELETE` | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | --- ## Authentication No standard auth is configured. Instead, an invalid token is passed manually via the `Cookie` header: | Header | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Cookie` | `token=invalid_random_string` | Intentionally invalid token to trigger a `403` response | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Declares the request body format | > ⚠️ An alternative approach (commented out in the pre-request script) is to set the `Cookie` header programmatically via `pm.request.headers.add(...)`. --- ## Pre-Request Script The pre-request script performs a prerequisite check before the request is sent: - **Step 1** — Asserts that the `bookingid` collection variable is set and not `undefined`. If this check fails, the test is aborted early to prevent false results. - **Step 2** _(commented out)_ — An alternative way to inject the invalid token via `pm.request.headers.add(...)` instead of using a hardcoded header. --- ## Tests | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1. Response status is 403 (Forbidden)` | Response status code must be exactly `403` | | `Test_2. Response time is below max_response_time` | Response time must be below the `max_response_time` collection variable (in milliseconds) | | `Test_3. Response body is NOT empty` | `Content-Type` must be `text/plain`; body must not be empty and must equal `"Forbidden"` | --- ## Variables Used | Variable | Scope | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL for the RESTful Booker API | | `131` | Collection | ID of the booking to be deleted (set by a prior create request) | | `1000` | Collection | Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds | --- ## Expected Behaviour - The API must return `403 Forbidden` when an invalid token is provided. - The response body must be the plain text string `"Forbidden"`. - The response must arrive within the threshold defined by `1000`.

# DeleteBooking (Invalid Booking ID) **Negative test** — attempts to delete a booking using a non-existent booking ID (`999999`) to verify that the API correctly rejects the request with a `405 Method Not Allowed` response. This test confirms the API's error-handling behaviour when an invalid resource ID is provided. --- ## Request Details | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Method** | `DELETE` | | **URL** | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/131` | --- ## Headers | Header | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Specifies the request payload format | | `Cookie` | `token=fd8b30247a7fb60` | Passes the auth token for protected endpoint access; alternative to the `Authorization` header | --- ## Variables | Variable | Source | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com` | Collection | Base URL of the RESTful Booker API | | `131` | Set in pre-request script | Overridden to `999999` to simulate a non-existent booking ID | | `fd8b30247a7fb60` | Collection variable | Auth token passed via the `Cookie` header | | `1000` | Collection variable | Maximum acceptable response time threshold (in milliseconds) | --- ## Pre-request Script Behaviour - **Step 1:** Sets `bookingid` to `999999` — a deliberately invalid/non-existent ID — to trigger an error response from the API. - **Step 2 (commented out):** An alternative approach that manually constructs and adds the `Cookie` header using `pm.request.headers.add` with the token retrieved from `pm.collectionVariables.get("token")`. This can be enabled if the header-based approach is not sufficient. --- ## Expected Response | Property | Expected Value | | --- | --- | | **Status code** | `405 Method Not Allowed` | | **Content-Type** | `text/plain` | | **Body** | `Method Not Allowed` | --- ## Test Coverage | Test | Assertion | | --- | --- | | `Test_1` — Status code | Response status is `405 Method Not Allowed` | | `Test_2` — Response time | Response time is below `1000` (collection variable) | | `Test_3` — Response body | Body is not empty, `Content-Type` is `text/plain`, and body equals `"Method Not Allowed"` |
